patch: Proposed registry additions used by Example 4 (market making across regime shifts)

Laws.doc: finite rational laws as values: (Indep L1 ... Lk) is the product law, whose values are k-tuples; (Image $v expr L) is the law of expr when $v is drawn from L, masses of equal values added; (Expect L) is the mean of a rational-valued law; (LawOf m) is the law of a declared Measure.  Coin and Point remain the elementary laws.  Laws are evaluated on their support, so a value of mass zero is never produced and carrier closure is checked on supports.

Monitors.doc: likelihood-ratio monitors for streams: a Monitor multiplies Alternative(c)(o) / Null(c)(o) over the observations o of a Stream, each read in the context c posted before it.  Exact claims about a monitor are Checked; detections on data are Estimated.

Kernel.doc: a map, or an instance of a parameterized map, from (Product States Actions) to (Law States)

RewardLaw.doc: a map or map instance from (Product States Actions) to (Law Rational)

Values.doc: value tolerance of the reward queries of the machine view

DecisionProcess.doc: a finite discounted decision process.  It is also a stochastic Machine whose observations are the expected rewards of its actions, one query (reward a) per action in declaration order, so InduceExact, CheckUpdates, MeasureBehavioral and CheckAbstractionMap apply to it unchanged; a quotient in that sense is an MDP homomorphism.

Context.doc: what is fixed before each observation, such as the posted quote

Null.doc: map or map instance from Context to the law of one observation

Columns.doc: (Columns [(context col+)] (observation col+)); (each col) reads every element of a list column as one observation

Stream.doc: frozen observation data with provenance; a different digest is a different stream

AverageModel.claim: prior-averaged reward law per action.  For a DecisionProcess with Through: the process on the codes whose rewards and pushed rows are averaged over each fiber under Under; admitted only when the hidden part is fresh (redrawn from Under at every step, independently of the rest), and then exact for every policy, history-dependent or not, that sees only the codes; InvalidInput otherwise

Compare.doc: Laws compares reward laws; Means compares expected rewards, which is what values and decisions of a risk-neutral process depend on

CheckEqual.claim: the two averaged reward laws are equal; for decision processes on the same states and actions (declared or averaged), equal kernels and equal reward laws (Compare Laws) or equal expected rewards (Compare Means), with witness the least state, the first action and the first successor or reward value, in increasing order, whose masses differ

OptimizePolicy.claim: optimal expected reward over policies that see only the representation.  For a DecisionProcess: the optimal discounted value from the start law Under, over stationary deterministic policies on states (no Through) or on codes (Through), evaluated in the concrete process, with the policy table and a Bellman certificate; on codes the class is memoryless code policies, which is every coarse policy when the hidden part is fresh

EvaluatePolicy.claim: exactly one of With and Policy.  With: expected reward of the best policy using the observation method, net of its cost; for a DecisionProcess the method reads the state component whose carrier is its channel's input once per step before the action, the policy also sees the code of Through, and values are computed on the hidden states, never by substituting the reading for the state.  Policy: the exact discounted value of the declared stationary policy from Under

CheckOptimal.claim: the stationary policy is optimal: its exact values V satisfy Q(x, pi x) >= Q(x, a) for every state and action, Q(x, a) = r(x, a) + gamma E V; Refuted with the least state, the policy's action, the first action in declaration order with a larger Q-value and the two exact Q-values

PullbackPolicy.claim: the arrow h is a homomorphism of decision processes (expected rewards and pushed rows preserved) and the policy x -> pi(h x) has at every source state the value pi has at h x; when h is surjective and pi is optimal for the target, the pulled-back policy is optimal for the source; Refuted with the homomorphism witness otherwise

CheckMonitor.claim: for every context the null expectation of the likelihood-ratio factor is at most one (exactly one when the alternative is absolutely continuous with respect to the null), so the product is a nonnegative supermartingale under the null for every policy that fixes the context before the observation; Blind when the two laws agree in every context; exact chi-square per context

Detect.claim: Estimated: if the stream follows the null laws, the probability that a listed monitor ever reaches its threshold is at most Level (Ville's inequality; Union gives each of k monitors the threshold k/Level, Mixture thresholds the average of the e-values at 1/Level); the result names the first monitor and observation to reach its threshold, or reports that none did, with the stream digest, the protocol and the dependence assumptions

OptimalityVerdict.doc: the exact values of the policy and the Q-table that certifies or refutes optimality

Detection.doc: an Estimated result: the claim is about the data source, never about the model
